claims.claim: 102 non-isomorphic ways of arranging zero to nine X's
claims.result: yes: 102 classes, Burnside gives 102; 46 of them have no line

claims.claim: Q = ⟨a,b,c,d | a²=1, b³=b, b²c=c, c³=ac², b²d=d, cd=ad, d²=c²⟩ has eighteen elements, the ones listed
claims.result: yes: the seven relations are already a complete rewriting system (21 critical pairs, none new); 18 normal forms

claims.claim: multiply the dictionary values; the sum is a P-position iff the product is in P = {a, b², bc, c²}
claims.result: yes, for sums of any size: a finite check over 285,480 states (15 kinds of board) proves it; plain search agrees on all 154,143,079 sums of up to 7 boards (0 mismatches)
yes: the products reach all 18 elements and no two elements behave alike in every context (0 pairs)

claims.claim: positions with too many completed rows are all assigned the identity
claims.result: yes: all 56 dead boards are 1 (and 3 live ones too)
forced: each of the 782 one-entry changes breaks the proof. (Q, P) has 4 automorphisms; 3 of them rename d and relabel the 4 d/ad entries, and those dictionaries work too

claims.claim: one board: the first player wins by playing in the centre
claims.result: yes; the empty board is c

claims.claim: …then wherever the second player plays, a knight's move away from that
claims.result: yes, as long as the knight's move does not complete a line (32 times one of the two would); whenever two such moves exist (8 times) both win

claims.claim: any move other than the centre loses: reply diametrically opposite, then rotate by 180°
claims.result: yes: centre is the only winning first move, and the rotation reply wins against all 8 other openings and every continuation

claims.claim: two empty boards: c², a second-player win
after a centre opening, copying it on the other board wins (c⁴ = c²)
claims.result: yes; after a corner or edge opening the copy loses (1·1 = 1). Of the 46 live boards, 26 are P when doubled

claims.claim: Figure 5 is an N-position and the copy (top-right of the right board) loses
claims.result: yes: ab, the copy makes 1. The winning replies: middle-left of the left board, middle-right of the left board, bottom-middle of the left board, bottom-right of the right board (the last one completes the diagonal)

claims.claim: the empty board is {2+, 0} and nim-heap 4 occurs as a single board (footnote)
claims.result: not checked (misère canonical forms are not implemented); the three boards with Grundy value 4 are exactly the ones valued d
